LESSON: CURVED MIRRORS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 3.1: Curved mirrors

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Curved mirrors. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are curved mirrors used in day-to-day life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe types of curved mirrors
2. draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors
3. describe the characteristics of images formed by concave and convex mirrors
4. explain the uses of concave and convex mirrors in day-to-day life
5. appreciate the applications of curved mirrors in
6. describe the generation of waves in nature
7. classify waves as longitudinal and transverse
8. describe basic characteristics of waves in nature

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CURVED MIRRORS
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Curved mirrors helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CURVED MIRRORS
Study Curved mirrors like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe types of curved mirrors

What this means
In this part you learn to describe types of curved mirrors. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe types of curved mirrors.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Curved mirrors” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe types of curved mirrors. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors

What this means
In this part you learn to draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Your turn

PART 6: Describe the generation of waves in nature

What this means

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the generation of waves in nature.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the generation of waves in nature. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Curved mirrors is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Curved mirrors” around your school. (skill: describe types of curved mirrors)

Example 2: Say why Curved mirrors matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Curved mirrors this week. (skill: describe the characteristics of images formed by concave and convex mirrors)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Curved mirrors” around your school. (skill: explain the uses of concave and convex mirrors in day-to-day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Curved mirrors to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe types of curved mirrors.
3. Practise this skill: draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors.
4. Practise this skill: describe the characteristics of images formed by concave and convex mirrors.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Curved mirrors from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Curved mirrors: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Curved mirrors?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are curved mirrors used in day-to-day life?
2. How are waves applied in our day-to- day life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Curved mirrors means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe types of curved mirrors.
5. Be able to: draw ray diagrams to locate images formed by concave and convex mirrors.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
